one_liner: ugrep-indexer builds Bloom-filter file indexes so ugrep's cold recursive search skips non-matching files, beating ripgrep.
what_it_does: ugrep is a GNU/BSD grep-compatible CLI search tool, drop-in via symlink to grep/egrep/fgrep. The companion ugrep-indexer utility pre-scans a directory tree and writes a hidden per-directory index file (`._UG#_Store`) of N-gram hashes for each file. `ugrep --index PATTERN` then consults these hashes before opening a file, skipping ones the index proves cannot match. Same CLI and regex engine as plain ugrep; indexing is an opt-in extra pass, not a different interface.
how_it_is_fast: ugrep-indexer builds a windowed N-gram hash table per file (Bloom-filter-like, tunable accuracy -0 to -9, default -4) using an additive prime-61 rolling hash over up to the first 16 bytes of the eventual search pattern, compiled by ugrep into a hash finite automaton (HFA) layered on top of its regex DFA. At search time ugrep tests each file's stored hash bits against the pattern's HFA before opening the file, so on a cold (uncached) filesystem it avoids the disk read and decompression cost for files that cannot match.
when_to_use: Recursive greps over directories that are cold in the OS page cache: network drives, rarely-touched archives, first search after mount/boot
Repeated searches of the same large, slowly-changing tree where the indexing pass amortizes over many searches
Patterns with a short, selective literal prefix (first 8-16 bytes distinctive) that keep the index false-positive rate low
Already using ugrep for its grep-compatible CLI, Unicode support, or archive/compressed-file search and want an extra lever for cold storage
Willing to spend ~0.5KB-14KB of index storage per file depending on chosen accuracy level
when_not_to_use: Files are already warm in the OS page cache -- indexing adds startup/check overhead and can be slower than a plain search
Highly volatile trees needing frequent re-indexing; re-indexing is incremental but still recurring maintenance work
Patterns using unlimited `*`/`+` repeats or large Unicode character classes -- these raise both index-hash construction start-up time and the false-positive rate
Need `-v` (invert), `--filter`, `-P` (Perl regex), or `-Z` (fuzzy) -- `--index` does not support these ugrep modes
Only one small, first-party benchmark exists (1,317 files/12.2MB on ugrep's own v3.12.6 tree); no independent or larger-scale confirmation

integration.dependencies: none required for core grep functionality; optional PCRE2 or Boost.Regex for -P (Perl regex), zlib for -z, and optional bzip2/lzma/lz4/zstd/brotli/bzip3 for specific compressed-archive formats
integration.min_toolchain: not documented -- autotools build (AC_PROG_CXX in configure.ac / ./build.sh), no pinned C++ standard flag found in configure.ac or src/Makefile.am
integration.platforms: Linux, macOS (Homebrew/MacPorts), Windows (winget), FreeBSD, OpenBSD, Alpine, Arch; x86-64 with SSE2/AVX2/AVX512BW auto-detected (disable via --disable-sse2/--disable-avx2), ARM/AArch64 NEON (--disable-neon to turn off)
integration.thread_safety: not documented as an explicit API guarantee; project runs ThreadSanitizer, AddressSanitizer, MemorySanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer in its dev workflow to catch data races, and search itself runs multi-threaded internally (8 threads in the benchmark)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial -- explain: plain ugrep is a drop-in replacement for grep/egrep/fgrep (via the `ug` symlink), but indexed mode is not drop-in for ripgrep's zero-setup usage -- it requires running ugrep-indexer ahead of time and passing --index

gotchas: Index has a false-positive (noise) rate -- some non-matching files are still opened; rate rises with permissive patterns and lower accuracy settings
Index files are hidden per-directory `._UG#_Store` files; use ugrep-indexer -d to remove them or re-index after large structural changes

Current --index design is safe (files are always re-scanned if newer than the index timestamp) only because indexes stay per-directory; the README explicitly warns a possible future 'single combined index file' option would drop that safety guarantee
Higher accuracy levels (-8/-9) push index storage up to tens of KB per very noisy file, versus ~4KB/file at the default -4
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Sibling entries (frg, ngi, trigrep) speed up ripgrep-class search on warm/in-memory data; ugrep+ugrep-indexer targets the opposite case -- cold, uncached filesystems -- and only pays off after a separate indexing pass, so pick it when your searches hit rarely-cached storage (network or cold disks) and you can tolerate index upkeep, not for ordinary warm-cache greps.
verified_claims_summary: On ugrep's own v3.12.6 source tree (1,317 files, 12.2MB, 8 threads), cold-filesystem search for 'std::chrono' took 1.02s unindexed vs 0.0487s best-of-4 (range 0.0487-0.0983s) with --index -- a 10x-21x self-comparison; ripgrep 13.0.0 took 1.18s on the same cold search (timed with shell `time`, vs ugrep's internal --stats timer), giving a derived roughly 12x-24x gap between indexed ugrep and ripgrep. No CPU, OS, or compiler flags are stated.
status_note: Core ugrep is actively maintained (3,302 stars, BSD-3-Clause, last commit 2026-09-15); the ugrep-indexer companion repo is smaller (84 stars) with its own last commit on 2025-06-22, so the indexing feature is iterating more slowly than core ugrep.
